script.title: Sydney Started Its Opera House Before Anyone Could Roof It
script.hook_text: Nobody knew how to roof it
sentences: Sydney started building an opera house nobody knew how to roof.
In 1957, Danish architect Jørn Utzon won the competition with a roof of curved shells.
The government pushed to start early anyway, and work began in 1959.
The engineers at Ove Arup & Partners couldn't find a way to build those shells.
No two roof forms repeated, so every piece would be a one-off.
They went through at least 12 versions.
In mid-1961 they made every shell a section of a sphere, so pieces could share one mould.
Even now, nobody agrees whose idea the sphere was.
script.description:
The Sydney Opera House roof had no workable design when construction began.
The fix came in 1961, from a sphere.
visuals: Sydney Opera House roof tiles close up
claims_en: Jørn Utzon, a Danish architect, won the design competition in 1957
The government pushed for work to begin early
Ove Arup & Partners were unable to find an acceptable solution to constructing the shells
There was no repetition in any of the roof forms, so precasting each individual section would have been expensive
The design team went through at least 12 iterations of the shell form
In mid-1961 the team found the solution of creating all the shells as sections from a sphere
This allowed arches of varying length to be cast in a common mould
Who exactly originated the solution has been the subject of controversy and the truth is unlikely ever to be categorically known
